cases.root_cause: The IB Gateway's API was briefly not accepting/answering connections for about 6 minutes before the open: the 09:10 option run started late (09:14:48) and failed with no SPX spot price, the retried 09:10 slot got a 'Socket disconnect' at 09:20:05, and both the 09:15 option and index runs failed with TimeoutError() after 4 s at 09:20:17. The exact reason for the Gateway being unavailable (e.g. a restart/login) is not visible in the run records — no IBKR codes and no Gateway log — so the cause is inferred from the failure chain; it recovered on its own by the next slot.

The 2026-10-15 afternoon equity_bars runs did not fail: each succeeded but reported missing_bars (700, and 500–650 earlier in the afternoon) because Alpaca did not return bars for part of the afternoon window. The 17:30 ET eod refetch re-pulled the day (17:30:36 run, 700 missing at the time of the incremental pull) and slo_status now shows 2026-10-15 equity bars 3,900/3,900 (SLI3 100%), so no bar data is lost. The day's only failures were on the IBKR side in the morning (09:14–09:20 ET), unrelated to equity bars.

The 09:10 option and index snapshot runs could not reach the IB Gateway's API: both failed their connect in ~4 s with a bare TimeoutError() (no IBKR error codes logged), which runbooks/gateway (section A) and runbooks/stale-snapshots define as "Gateway API not accepting connections". A one-off connect failure at the 09:10 slot (the only failed IBKR runs on the day; equity_bars, which uses Alpaca, was 90/90 and never affected) fits the morning secdef-stall pattern, but the runs do not record what state the Gateway was in, so the exact cause (secdef stall / wedged Gateway vs. a connect timeout) is not proven by the data.

The data doesn't support a single confirmed cause. On 2026-10-16 only the 09:10:02 option and index slots failed (both TimeoutError() after 4 s, the signature of a Gateway connect timeout), and the option timeliness SLI of 60.26% (26 of 78 slots late, coverage still 100%) shows that morning's slots ran late. But the tool results I have don't show any option or index run starting or finishing between 09:50 and 10:41, so nothing in them explains what caused a gap of that length at that time — no post-09:10 failure, no stuck run, no IBKR error codes. The late slots and the 09:10 failure look different from the two documented incidents: 2026-10-23 was a secdef stall with one 7-minute delay, and 2026-10-26 lost all 78 option slots, while here all 78 succeeded. I can't rule out a queue backlog behind a long-running option run (max_active_runs=1), a stuck run, or a Gateway problem I can't see, so I'm not asserting any of them. The one real failure is a Gateway connect timeout at 09:10:02 (runbooks/gateway section A), but it recovers at the next slot. Please run the triage in runbooks/stale-snapshots step 2–3 (dags list-runs plus the pipeline_runs error tail) to see the morning's actual run timings and confirm whether a run was stuck. Don't propose a Gateway reconnect: no run shows persistent farm-disconnect codes (1100/2103/2105/2157), so the runbook doesn't call for it.

One equity_bars run (the 10:09 slot) was cut off by an Alpaca transport failure: RemoteProtocolError('Server disconnected without sending a response.') after 18 s. It was a one-off vendor API drop, not a pipeline or Gateway problem: the next slots succeeded normally, no bars went missing, and the day's equity bar SLI is 100%.

The 09:20:01 option_snapshots run hit its 8-minute execution timeout: it was killed at exactly 480 s, which the pipeline records as status=failed with an empty error field — hence "no error message". It was a one-off, confined to that slot: the rest of 2026-10-19 was normal (all 82 index_snapshots runs succeeded, option_snapshots ended 83 runs with only this one failure, bars 3900/3900), so the data does not show a Gateway outage, a farm disconnect or a secdef stall behind it.

Codes 10090 (not subscribed for this instrument) and 10167 (delayed data instead of live) on the 2026-10-19 option snapshot runs are IBKR market-data entitlement messages for the collector username, raised per contract/chain (they recur only on the ~3-min, 2333-2353-row runs), not a gateway outage: the session kept 78/78 option slots and index runs were clean. The 354 belongs to the same subscription family. No data was lost that day, so this is a subscription/permissions caveat rather than an incident. The 09:38 start time and the failed 09:20:01 run cannot be attributed from the available records.

No sessions were lost: 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 were collected on the Mac, but this host's pipeline_runs holds no run records for them (collection moved to the Windows host around 2026-10-27), so slo_status reads 0/78 option slots for both days. The data exists — ops/slo.md's session table shows 10-22 at 100 % coverage and 10-23 at 100 % coverage but 94.9 % on-time (secdef stall incident), and equity bars read 100 % for both days from staged data, which confirms the snapshots are there but unrecorded.

IBKR's contract-definition (secdef) server stopped answering for about 5 minutes from 10:35 ET on Friday 2026-10-23. Every snapshot run made contract-definition requests (qualifyContracts, reqSecDefOptParams) before its first quote request, so the option run hung on its first chain (spx_monthly) until RequestTimeout (300 s), burned its 6-min run budget, and failed; the retry succeeded 7 min late and pushed the next four slots back (max_active_runs=1). The index run got no answer at all and was killed by its 2-min task timeout on both attempts, so the 10:35 index snapshot was lost. Market-data farms were fine (no farm errors, quotes flowed) and Alpaca equity bars were unaffected.

The 08:15 ET `contract_cache` refresh began re-listing every cached expiry (~24 MB / ~23k messages), which overloaded IBKR's contract-definition (secdef) service and broke the market-data farms (2103 hfarm at 08:22:44). By ~09:16 the Gateway's API port stopped accepting connections at all, and IBC's RESTART could not revive it (the Gateway UI was wedged too); only a container restart with a full 2FA login at 19:40 brought it back. Option and index snapshot runs all failed for the rest of the session. No evidence of a competing login: the 08:15:42 1100/1102 kept the same session ("data maintained").

Both days show the same symptom — the 09:10 option and index snapshot slots failing with a 4-second `TimeoutError()` (a connect timeout) — and both recovered by themselves: every later slot succeeded, so neither day repeats the 2026-10-23 secdef stall or the 2026-10-26 wedge. That signature matches an IB Gateway that was momentarily unreachable (typically a restart/login at 09:05 waiting for the 2FA push, as on 2026-10-16), but no tool result exposes a Gateway log, an error code, or a ConnectTimeout detail for 09:10 on either day, so the record cannot confirm the Gateway restart and cannot separate 10-27 from 10-30.

Routine IBKR reconnect: the option run saw 1100 (connectivity lost) and 2103 (market-data farm down), then 1102/2110 indicate the farm/session was restored. All 78 option slots on 2026-11-05 succeeded, nothing was lost. Runbook gateway section D says a 1100 followed by 1102 with data maintained needs no action.

Nothing is wrong with the Gateway. The 2157 (and 2103) codes on option runs are routine IBKR data-farm drops that recover within the same run; those runs complete successfully. Only the 2026-11-10 early-morning runs (a separate event, around 09:25 ET) actually failed.

The IB Gateway's API refused/timed out every connection from ~09:10 to ~09:26 on 2026-11-10 (connect TimeoutError() after ~4 s on both option_snapshots and index_snapshots). The four queued 5-minute slots (09:10, 09:15, 09:20, 09:25) each waited while the outage lasted, so they all fired together at 09:25:15–09:26:03 and failed. The 09:25 option run additionally reported ConnectionError('Socket disconnect')/'Not connected' on every chain with codes 2104/2106/2119/2158, consistent with the API connection dropping. Recovery happened by itself around 09:30; the rest of the session ran normally (option coverage 78/78, on-time 98.72%). The pipeline_runs evidence does not show why the Gateway refused connections (no Gateway/IBC logs, no 2FA or login signal, no 1100→1102 sequence, no 2103/2105/2157 farm break), so gateway_frozen is only the closest match, not a proven cause.

The data volume filled up: every dataset's tasks now fail instantly with OSError(28) 'No space left on device' before writing anything (runs end in 2 s). Nothing points to the Gateway — the last runs that still wrote data (IBKR and Alpaca clients) were fine, and the error is a local filesystem ENOSPC on the write path shared by all datasets.

Collection is not affected: the dbt build failed because another process (python3.12, PID 4127) held an open handle on /opt/airflow/data/curated.duckdb, and DuckDB allows only one writer and refuses even read-only opens while a writer is connected. Something (a notebook, DuckDB CLI/UI, SQL client, or a stale earlier dbt) was left open on the curated file at the 17:30 ET build.

Every equity_bars and daily_bars run on 2026-11-12 failed within ~1 s with Alpaca HTTP 401 Unauthorized on https://data.alpaca.markets/v2/stocks/bars — an Alpaca API-key/auth failure, not an IBKR or collection problem. No slot succeeded (0 successful equity_bars runs today), so no bars were written for 11-12 or for the 10-session window of the 17:30 eod refetch.

The collector's IBKR user is getting no live option quotes because a second session of the same user is holding the live market-data subscription (IBKR code 10197). The Gateway connection itself is healthy — option and index runs still connect, finish on time and return rows — but IBKR delivers bid/ask for none of the contracts, so the snapshots are structurally empty (no_quote 3400, zero two-sided quotes).

The host/scheduler was not running for the whole of 2026-11-12: pipeline_runs has zero rows for that day (success or failed), so no slot ever started — not even the Alpaca equity-bar runs, which don't touch the Gateway, and the EOD runs at 17:30. That rules out a Gateway/IBKR fault (it would leave failing runs and cards) and, since no run or card was produced at all, also missing_run_records. The hardware/stack needs checking; data for 11-12 is lost for option quotes (no backfill).

IBKR's contract-definition (secdef) service stopped answering during the 08:15 contract_cache refresh, so the 08:20 Gateway check's `合约查询` field timed out (20 s) and the pre-open option runs' contract-definition requests hung until the 6-min run budget was spent: `spx_monthly` raised `TimeoutError()` and `spx_weekly` was skipped, so every chain failed. It was not session-wide: the Gateway recovered before the open (09:30 onward all slots succeeded), and no 'Login has completed' / 2FA sequence is visible in the runs as recall item 2 would imply.

Six consecutive option_snapshot slots (11:00–11:25) each ran the full 480 s execution budget and were killed, with no error recorded. Index snapshots kept succeeding throughout (4–5 s runs, 0 failures all day), so the Gateway API port was accepting connections and answering requests: the failure was confined to the option collection task, where requests hung until the run budget expired (the 2026-10-23 pattern, and the reason no error text was written). The data available does not distinguish a secdef/contract-cache stall from a single hung request after a connectivity loss, so the exact trigger is not established.

IBKR market-data farms were disconnected (codes 2103 and 2105) during the 13:00–13:25 ET window, so the collector got no SPX spot quote for the underlying and every option-snapshot slot failed with "SPX: no spot price". The outage cleared on its own, most likely after the RECONNECTDATA the failing runs (and the watchdog) sent; runs from 13:30 ET on succeeded again. The Gateway itself stayed up: index_snapshots kept succeeding throughout via cached values, i.e. no subscription problem and no paused Gateway.

IB Gateway was not logged in for the 09:10–10:15 window: it was still in the login/2FA phase (Second Factor Authentication initiated 08:58, "Login has completed" only at 10:17), so the API port refused connections and every option and index snapshot failed its connect with TimeoutError() after 4 s. Runs recovered on their own at the next slot after the login completed; the Gateway was not wedged and no data farms were in error. Why the login took ~79 minutes is not visible in the tools — the 2FA push simply wasn't approved for that long (IBC retries the login every 180 s, runbook E step 3), but the logs that would confirm the retries aren't in these results.

No data is lost: the intraday equity_bars runs on 2026-11-12 all succeeded but reported missing_bars = 450 (50 symbols' worth), i.e. Alpaca served no bars for the window from about 12:35-12:45 ET onward, while every run from 12:45 to 16:25 completed in 9-21 s with rows growing normally (rows 2600 at 14:05 … 3450 at 16:25) and no errors. The end-of-day refetch at 17:30:01-17:31:14 ET returned 3900 rows per session for every session in the refetch window (11-12, 11-10, 11-09, 11-06, 11-05, 11-04, 11-03, 11-02, 10-30, 10-29) and all 90 runs of the day succeeded, so the window appears recovered; only slo_status still reports 11-12 at 3450/3900 bars (88.46%), which is the pre-refetch metric reading. Worth confirming the eod-refetched rows landed in curated before closing, and confirming it was Alpaca's feed rather than ours, as on 2026-10-15.

One IBKR request in the 11:00:00 option snapshot run hung after an 1100 connectivity loss (followed by 1102), so the run sat until its 300 s execution timeout and failed with TimeoutError(); because option snapshots run with max_active_runs=1, the slots queued behind it (11:05–11:30) each started only when the previous run ended, so that window ran late until the schedule caught up. Index snapshots (separate 4–5 s runs) and Alpaca equity bars were unaffected, and the Gateway itself stayed up.
